description.en: Like the third part on Moodle: one case description and four diagrams about it (class, use case, sequence, implementation). Solutions drawn for SeisHub.

question.en:
You are asked to model an object-oriented system for a company that manages a chain of car dealerships. Each dealership sells cars. The company employs sales representatives who are responsible for showing cars and conducting test drives, as well as for sales, and technicians who are responsible for car maintenance. The company maintains the following information for its employees: first name, last name, year of birth, place of birth, ID number, and salary points. Additionally, for sales representatives, information on the percentage of monthly turnover they have achieved is maintained, and for technicians, information on completed specialist courses is kept.

The company has its own website through which clients can search the cars offered by the company. The search is performed by specifying the type of car, the type of fuel, and the maximum price of the car, after which a list of cars that meet the criteria is provided. The client can select a specific car, and additional information about the car is displayed. The additional information is displayed in the following format: car code, type and name of the car, year of manufacture, number of doors, type of fuel, maximum engine capacity, car photo, additional description, car price, and a list of dealerships (their addresses) where the car is available for sale. If the client shows interest in a car, they can schedule an appointment to view the car and test drive it. When scheduling an appointment, the client needs to provide their personal details (first name, last name, ID number, date of birth, address, and contact phone), select the dealership they will visit, select a date for viewing the car and test driving it. After that, the system returns possible appointment times based on the availability of the sales representatives. The client then selects one of the times and clicks the SCHEDULE button.

After viewing and test driving the car, the client may decide to purchase a certain car. If the client decides to purchase, the sales representative must create a purchase contract for the car. This is done by selecting the car from the list of unsold cars that the client is interested in. Then, the client's information is filled out, and the purchase date, sale price, and warranty duration are recorded. By clicking the CREATE CONTRACT button, a purchase contract is printed in three copies, and the system generates the invoice that needs to be issued to the customer. The invoice should state the car's price, any discounts, the method of payment, and the total amount due. After this, the customer is issued a fiscal receipt for the paid service, the keys are handed over, and the dealership's data is updated regarding the sale of the car.

The company has its own dealerships in several cities in the country (Skopje – 3; Bitola, Kumanovo, Ohrid, and Shtip – 1 each). In Skopje, there are three dealerships (Center, Gjorce Petrov, and Aerodrom). The central server (which hosts the web application and the database) of the company is located in the dealership in Aerodrom. Each dealership accesses this central server through which car sales and employee work are conducted. In addition to the internet, clients can also schedule an appointment to view a car through terminals placed in the company's dealerships. Each dealership has 2 offices equipped with 5 personal computers each (used by the company's employees) and one printer per office. Additionally, each dealership has a separate computer with a fiscal device.
Draw the class diagram of the system for the car dealership company. (10 pts)
